rows.statusBasis: biome.json:10-21 IS the cited enforcer — the files.ignore array itself (.next, node_modules, dist, out, supabase/.temp, supabase/.branches, apps/mobile/android, apps/mobile/ios, dim-interno:docs/design/handoffs/**, dim-interno:docs/reviews/results/**). Nothing reads it back; rg for `biome.json` under __tests__/scripts/e2e returns only the application-fence pair, which parses the overrides array, never files.ignore.
rows.notes: Self-executing declaration, true at this SHA. The previous basis conceded the point in its own note — 'a scope declaration cannot fail on its own' — and still recorded ENFORCED; under R2 that is UNENFORCED.

rows.rule: noUnusedVariables and noUnusedImports must be errors project-wide, with an override list of files where they are turned off.
rows.statusBasis: biome.json:59-62 sets correctness.noUnusedVariables and noUnusedImports to "error"; package.json:79 verify runs `pnpm lint`. Two override blocks turn them off for enumerated files (biome.json:389-402 noUnusedImports for 5 files; :404-493 noUnusedVariables for ~79) — the rule text itself provides for that list.
rows.notes: Brief's explicit R2 carve-out: biome rules at level error with lint in verify ARE enforcers. The override list is not ratcheted by any fence, but the rule text names it as legitimate. Same conclusion as the previous basis.

rows.rule: Native-facing code must never read `next/headers` cookies for identity — `/api/v1` authentication resolves identity strictly from the Authorization header via `createClientFromBearer` → `requireLiveUser`, with no cookie fallback; a refusal returns 401 + a code, never a redirect.
rows.statusBasis: No fence scans app/api/v1 for next/headers or cookies(): the only scripts/check-*.ts that names next/headers is check-application-fence.ts, whose corpus is src/modules/*/application/**. check-api-guard-headers.ts bans middleware-STAMPED headers, a different subject. Per-route tests use createClientFromBearer, but none asserts the absence of a cookie path as a rule over the surface.
rows.notes: A cheap fence exists in shape (the v1 route glob is already pinned at check-api-v1-envelope.ts:58 with a floor of 33 files) but no rule for cookies was added to it.

rows.rule: Every use-case graduating into `src/modules/<domain>/application/` must accept a plain-data input (never FormData, Request, or Headers) and return a plain-data, JSON-serializable result, signaling failure through typed discriminated results rather than throwing for expected domain conditions.
rows.statusBasis: check-application-fence.ts restricts IMPORTS (next, next/cache, next/navigation, next/headers, server-only, @/lib/supabase/server) — it never inspects a use-case's parameter or return TYPE. FormData and Request are global types needing no import, so the fence cannot see them.
rows.notes: A real gap: the import fence is often read as covering this rule, and it structurally cannot.

rows.rule: New or touched use-case error branches should carry a stable, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE error code alongside the human-facing message, not a bare Spanish string.
rows.statusBasis: No fence inspects UseCaseResult's failure arm. packages/contract/src/api/errors.ts:17-20 says so explicitly: 'It is not a repair of UseCaseResult's failure arm, which is an untyped string carrying Spanish prose in most of the ten module copies'.
rows.notes: The rule is stated as 'should', and the contract package's own header records that the failure arm is untyped today.

rows.rule: Future /api/v1 pagination must be cursor-based (keyset), never offset-based.
rows.statusBasis: The cited __tests__/keyset-pagination.test.ts is a UNIT test of lib/keyset-pagination.ts's pure helpers (:1-8: encode/decode roundtrip, tampered input, keysetWhere shape, olderHref/newerHref). It proves the helper works; it never enumerates /api/v1 routes and cannot fail on an offset-paginated one. Refuter pattern 2.
rows.notes: The ADR cites the test as a PRECEDENT, and draft 1 read the citation as enforcement.

rows.rule: Any new /api/v1 event-writing route requires an Idempotency-Key header mapped to pet_events.client_idempotency_key, deduped via the pet_events_idempotency_idx partial unique index.
rows.statusBasis: Reusing the refuter: __tests__/idempotency-guards.test.ts is per-use-case (createIntake :172, createTattooForUser :244, createVaccineReminder :301, FosterRepository :361, confirmChipMatch* :411/:455); it never globs app/api/v1/** and never asserts the header is required. Per-route tests exist (api-v1-amend, api-v1-record-event, api-v1-lost, api-v1-shares) but no route-enumerating fence.
rows.notes: The DB half (pet_events_idempotency_idx partial unique index) is a live constraint; the ROUTE half is what is unenforced.

rows.rule: requirePetAccess/requireAlivePetAccess must remain the single security boundary for pet-scoped operations regardless of transport (cookie or bearer token) — no second auth model.
rows.statusBasis: check-authz-guards.ts lists requirePetAccess/requireAlivePetAccess among 20+ accepted AUTH_GUARDS (:80-81) — it accepts ANY of them, so a route that invented a second pet-access model and listed it would simply be added to the list. Nothing asserts these two are the ONLY pet-scoped boundary.
rows.notes: check-titular-gate.ts enforces a narrower, related rule (role inside the ownership row) and does discover by EFFECT — the shape this rule would need.

rows.rule: The public-token-resolves-to-QR-page path must stay anonymous — it needs no auth from web or native clients.
rows.statusBasis: A 'must stay open' rule has no failing predicate in this repo's fences, which all detect MISSING guards. check-authz-guards.ts would accept the public route either way (a `// @no-auth-required` comment satisfies it, and so would adding a guard).
rows.notes: The throttle-coverage fence (CANON-309) covers the adjacent requirement that the anonymous path be rate-limited.

rows.rule: Push notifications must stay transport-agnostic: use-cases collect plain-data NewNotification[] with no transport-specific fields; only the action layer chooses the delivery transport.
rows.statusBasis: scripts/check-notifications-service.ts enforces the WRITE PATH (no new direct .insert(notifications); go through createNotification/createNotificationsBulk) — not the payload's transport neutrality. Nothing inspects NewNotification fields for a web-only URL scheme.
rows.notes: Stated as a review question ('fitness hook'), not as a mechanical predicate.

rows.rule: Anchor `lib/ui/audit-filters.ts` date filters at Argentine midnight (fixed -03:00, no DST), never at UTC midnight.
rows.statusBasis: lib/ui/audit-filters.ts:62 does it right (`new Date(`${raw}T00:00:00.000-03:00`)`, PO decision noted at :56) but the implementation is not an enforcer. __tests__/audit-filter-options.test.ts covers only buildAuditActionOptions labels/aliases (:17-64) — nothing asserts the -03:00 anchor. lint:timezone's corpus is toLocaleDateString/toLocaleString/Intl.DateTimeFormat calls, not date PARSING.
rows.notes: Same shape as the refuter's CANON-202: the correct helper exists, nothing fails if someone reverts it.

rows.rule: The pet-photo upload flow must land a signed upload in a private bucket, then re-authorize, verify magic bytes and re-encode in a `confirm` step before writing to the public bucket.
rows.statusBasis: __tests__/pet-photo-upload.test.ts:240 asserts the minted ticket's bucket is STAGING_BUCKET (the private uploads-staging); :269-283 confirm refuses SVG/HTML/ZIP by sniffing and removes the staged object; :313 fails closed when sharp throws (never the original bytes); :322 stores the RE-ENCODED bytes under a key derived from the sniffed type; :364 and :394 re-authorize at confirm (soft-deleted pet, erasure mid-transaction) and take back what was written.
rows.notes: Also :205-232 the staged-path prefix-equality guard, so a confirm cannot promote another pet's staged object.

rows.rule: An anonymous denuncia's rate-limiter bucket key must not leak the caller's user id into an unbounded reader population; `redactCallerId` closes this and reverting it must turn a test red.
rows.statusBasis: __tests__/api-v1-welfare-reports-route.test.ts:935 asserts the fail-open error report does NOT contain the caller uuid (ME), with non-vacuity at :938 that the bucket+window text ('welfare_auth:«caller»:hour:') survives — so deleting redactCallerId (app/api/v1/welfare-reports/commands.ts:490,507) turns it red.
rows.notes: The claim the doc makes about the test is verifiable and true — rare in this corpus.

rows.rule: A `/api/v1` route must answer only through `apiV1Json`/`apiV1Error` (lib/infra/api-v1.ts) — never NextResponse.json(, new NextResponse(, new Response(, or Response.json( directly.
rows.statusBasis: scripts/check-api-v1-envelope.ts:303-316 fails the four hand-built spellings and a missing apiV1Json/apiV1Error import over 33 routes (floor :246). But the fence's own header at :45-49 declares the hole: 'a response built in a helper module the route imports (the fence reads the route file only)' — a route that imports the helper and delegates one branch to a wrapper still answers outside apiV1Json, which the rule's 'answers ONLY through' clause forbids.
rows.notes: live MIN_V1_ROUTE_FILES = 33. The previous basis rates this ENFORCED on :305/:312/:246 and does not address the stated blind spot at :45-49, which I opened; the hole is narrow (the import check catches a route that never touches the helper) but it is self-declared and inside the rule's scope

rows.rule: Every `/api/v1` route must be rate-limited with a literal (not computed) bucket name — including any `perLookup.bucket` — and its fail-open/fail-closed direction must be stated.
rows.statusBasis: scripts/check-api-v1-envelope.ts:319-330 fails a non-literal surface bucket and a non-literal perLookup.bucket, but only WHERE publicTokenThrottle/perLookup already appear — no check requires a /api/v1 route to be rate-limited at all, and nothing asserts the fail-open/closed direction is stated (rg over the fence and __tests__/public-token-throttle-coverage.test.ts finds no such assertion).
rows.notes: the throttle test (:553-720) covers public-token resolvers, not every v1 route (/auth/login, /me)

rows.rule: Every /api/v1 response carrying pet, case, denuncia or share data must set cache-control: no-store explicitly — the middleware prefix allowlist does not cover /api/v1.
rows.statusBasis: lib/infra/api-v1.ts:40-43,58-61 sets cache-control: no-store LAST, after any caller headers, so no route can override it. scripts/check-api-v1-envelope.ts:303-307 fails a v1 route that does not import the helper and :308-315 fails any hand-built response (NextResponse.json/new NextResponse/new Response/Response.json), over globSync("app/api/v1/**/route.ts") (:58) with a non-vacuity route-count floor (:342). pnpm lint:api-v1 is in verify (package.json:79).
rows.notes: P15 single-door shape: the fence mandates the helper, so the helper's guarantee reaches every route rather than only its own test.

rows.rule: /api/v1 errors must use the { error: "snake_case_code" } envelope with a code from the agreed vocabulary.
rows.statusBasis: lib/infra/api-v1.ts:72-79 — apiV1Error(code: ApiV1ErrorCode, …) builds `const body: ApiV1Error = { error: code }`, a single-key envelope whose code is typed against @dim/contract/api (:36), so an invented code fails typecheck (verify gate #2). scripts/check-api-v1-envelope.ts:303-315 forbids any v1 route from answering except through that helper, so no route can hand-roll a different error shape.
rows.notes: snake_case-ness of a NEWLY added vocabulary member is not itself asserted anywhere I opened; the closed union is what makes the code set closed. The previous basis records the same caveat (CANON-344).

rows.rule: Every section of a /api/v1 read must report its own availability; nothing may degrade to a silent empty section.
rows.statusBasis: check-api-v1-envelope.ts has exactly three rules — response helper, literal limiter bucket, authorization — and none inspects payload section shape. No test enumerates v1 read sections for an availability flag.
rows.notes: scripts/check-degraded-chrome.ts enforces the analogous rule for server components, not for /api/v1 payloads.

rows.rule: Every /api/v1 read must carry payloadVersion, issuedAt, and staleAfter.
rows.statusBasis: apiV1Envelope exists and is proved by __tests__/api-v1.test.ts:65-84, but nothing REQUIRES a read route to call it: check-api-v1-envelope.ts mentions the three fields only in its motivation header (:10) and its import check names apiV1Json/apiV1Error only (:305). A read route that skipped apiV1Envelope would pass every gate.
rows.notes: Asymmetry worth naming: the no-store and error-envelope halves ARE structurally enforced (CANON-332/333) because they live in the two helpers the fence requires; the read envelope lives in a third helper the fence does not require.

rows.rule: Success and failure responses must be indistinguishable wherever an oracle exists, proven by a response-equality test per oracle.
rows.statusBasis: __tests__/denuncia-access-timing-oracle.test.ts:156-190 proves response equality (message, throttled, and the latency arm) for ONE oracle — solicitarAccesoDenunciaAction. Nothing enumerates the other oracle surfaces or requires a response-equality test per oracle; the 'wherever an oracle exists' half rests on the merge checklist in docs/architecture/api-invariants.md, which no fence reads.
rows.notes: Subset covered: the denuncia oracle. Draft 1 read the doc's 'reference test shape' citation as coverage of the general rule.

rows.rule: Any route resolving a public token must go through publicPetByToken so the coverage fence can see it.
rows.statusBasis: __tests__/public-token-throttle-coverage.test.ts:277 — the census IS `allSources().filter(includes('publicPetByToken('))`, so it only grades files that already spell the door. The file records twice that a resolver using a hand-rolled `eq(pets.publicToken, …)` is invisible to it: :681-684 ("It was never exempt; it was INVISIBLE") and :692-694. Nothing fails when a route skips the door.
rows.notes: Rule predicate IS adoption of a single door; no P15-style structural mandate exists. The ALIAS census (:1124) closes only the second NAME, not raw drizzle resolution. The v3 basis concedes the same gap ('a route that resolved a token by another path would be invisible to it') and then credits the alias pin with closing it — the alias pin bans one spelling, not the unnamed path the file's own :681-694 note describes.

rows.rule: Any route resolving a chip or a DNI must carry its own rate limiter — lookupByChip and verifyDni bring none by design.
rows.statusBasis: The throttle-coverage fence keys on publicPetByToken( call sites, not on lookupByChip/verifyDni. No fence derives a chip/DNI corpus, and check-api-v1-envelope.ts's limiter rule only bans a computed bucket where a limiter already exists.
rows.notes: This is the exact defect shape the public-token fence was built for, on a corpus the fence does not cover.

rows.rule: Any route accepting an upload must go through lib/infra/uploads.ts — a signed upload URL may never point at a public bucket without replicating magic-byte sniffing, the no-SVG whitelist and server-side re-encoding first; the storage key must be derived from validated MIME + randomUUID(), never the client filename.
rows.statusBasis: __tests__/pet-photo-upload.test.ts:189-350 fences ONE door (lib/infra/pet-photo-upload.ts): whitelist parity, no SVG, magic bytes, sharp re-encode, key from validated MIME + minted uuid. No fence enumerates upload entry points or requires a route to reach lib/infra/uploads.ts (rg 'uploads' over scripts/check-*.ts returns only storage-grant and scheduled-ref scripts), and other doors exist unfenced — app/api/v1/welfare-reports/route.ts evidence uploads, src/modules/events/actions.ts, app/org/[orgToken]/atender/actions.ts.
rows.notes: Corroboration only, not an enforcer (P17 trap the basis flagged): scripts/check-storage-write-policies.ts:193 records that closing B24 needs 'moving the ~30 Server-Action upload sites onto the signed upload primitive' and that the caller migration 'has not happened'.

rows.rule: Any /api/v1 route that mutates must accept an Idempotency-Key header and replay the first outcome for a repeated key.
rows.statusBasis: Same shape as CANON-323 and consistent with the refuter's verdict there: per-route tests exercise the header (api-v1-amend, api-v1-record-event, api-v1-lost, api-v1-shares, api-v1-pets, api-v1-me-caretaker-grants) but nothing enumerates the mutating v1 routes and requires it. check-api-v1-envelope.ts has no idempotency rule.

rows.rule: DNI lookup must stay deliberately unthrottled; the only mitigation is collapsing the unique-violation and generic-failure branches into the same message.
rows.statusBasis: The message-collapse half is a code fact stated in a comment, not an assertion: no test compares the two branches' strings. Nothing would fail if one branch were given a distinguishable message, which is the whole risk the rule names.
rows.notes: Compare CANON-342/343, where the analogous denuncia oracle IS pinned by a response-equality test.

rows.rule: The denuncia code-access endpoint must return one NEUTRAL_MESSAGE constant on every branch and rate-limit at 5/min + 20/hr per IP, fail-closed.
rows.statusBasis: __tests__/denuncia-access-timing-oracle.test.ts:48-52 mocks enforceRateLimit to `async () => undefined`, so the 5/min + 20/hr fail-closed half — declared live at app/(public)/denuncias/codigo/[code]/actions.ts:85-92 — has no assertion anywhere; the neutral-message half is pinned at :180-183 (every branch's message equals the matching branch's).
rows.notes: Live maxPerMinute 5 / maxPerHour 20 at actions.ts:86-87; the non-RateLimitError rethrow at :91 is the fail-closed arm, also unasserted. The mocked limiter (:48-52) is stronger evidence than the v3 basis's 'no limiter-constant pin was found'.

rows.rule: Denuncia redemption must return the same 303 to the same URL on success and failure, differing only in whether a cookie is set, and must compare tokens with timingSafeEqual behind a length guard.
rows.statusBasis: The timingSafeEqual-behind-a-length-guard half is fenced: lib/infra/denuncia-reporter-token.ts:131-132 guards the length, and lib/infra/denuncia-reporter-token.test.ts:48-74 asserts garbage/empty/MAC-tampered input returns false instead of throwing. The 303 half is not: app/(public)/denuncias/seguimiento/entrar/route.ts:53,59,61-67 has no test, and the cited denuncia-access-timing-oracle.test.ts:156 is the access-REQUEST action, not redemption.
rows.notes: No test file asserts a 303 for the redemption route; the four test files mentioning 303 are lost-view-model, govt-dashboards, location and turnos. The v3 basis states its assertions were not read line by line.

rows.rule: Error codes for /api/v1 must be lowercase_snake and live in packages/contract.
rows.statusBasis: lib/infra/api-v1.ts:36 types apiV1Error against ApiV1ErrorCode from @dim/contract/api, so a route cannot invent a code — __tests__/api-v1.test.ts:54-63 keeps that non-vacuous with a @ts-expect-error on "made_up_code". The casing half has no check: nothing in packages/contract/src/api/errors.ts or check-api-v1-envelope.ts matches the union members against /^[a-z0-9_]+$/, so a PascalCase entry added to the array compiles.
rows.notes: errors.ts:7-8 records lowercase_snake as the D2 decision in prose only, and quotes 34 as a 2026-08 handler census — a header number, not a live pin (P17), so number stays null. Basis agrees on both points.

rows.rule: The /api/v1 credential payload must project only fields the page actually renders, never the loader's full fetched shape (it must exclude the microchip number, full vaccination history rows, and internal UUIDs).
rows.statusBasis: The payload shape lives in a Zod/TS type in packages/contract, so a WIDENING of that type compiles fine — tsc cannot object to publishing more. No fence compares the payload's field set against the page's rendered field set, and no test asserts the three named exclusions.
rows.notes: A derivation discipline recorded in prose; the failure mode it names (project the loader's type) would pass every gate.

rows.rule: Redaction must run before the sink is handed anything, so no provider adapter can leak by forgetting to scrub — redaction must never move behind the sink interface.
rows.statusBasis: lib/observability/redact.ts and its two tests prove WHAT redaction removes, not WHERE it sits in the call order. No fence asserts that every sink call site is downstream of redact(), and the sink itself is a pending PO decision, so there is no adapter to fence yet.
rows.notes: Pending PO decision.

rows.rule: Redaction must cover DNI, all twelve product credential-code prefixes, care-grant tokens, emails, phones, JWTs, Authorization headers, capability tokens in URL path segments, and sensitive query-string values.
rows.statusBasis: redact-prefix-coverage.test.ts:88-95 fails when any minted prefix is uncovered and :109-145 when any capability route segment is; redact.test.ts:17-90 pins DNI (7 and 8 digit), emails, phones, :59 care-grant CG-, :153 JWT, :166 Authorization header, :173 query-string value. Every named vocabulary item has a failing assertion.
rows.notes: CREDENTIAL_TOKEN_PREFIXES in lib/observability/redact.ts:79-92 lists exactly 12; the fence asserts minted.size >= 12 at :85, so 12 is a derived floor rather than a pinned constant. Basis agrees.

rows.rule: The redactor's prefix list and capability-segment list must be re-derived from source (drift-fenced), never hand-maintained.
rows.statusBasis: redact-prefix-coverage.test.ts:52-64 re-derives the prefix set by scanning source for generatePrefixedToken("X") plus the welfare generator; :88 fails on uncovered, :97 on orphaned (both directions), :109-145 re-derives capability segments from the router glob. :75-86 is the fence's own smoke test (DIM/CAS/FP/DEN + size>=12) so the regexes cannot rot into a vacuous pass.
rows.notes: Basis agrees, same lines.

rows.rule: The error-report context object must be a closed allowlist — an unreviewed field is a compile error at the call site and is dropped at runtime.
rows.statusBasis: No ClientErrorContext / ErrorReportContext type was found under lib/, packages/ or __tests__/, so the closed-allowlist type the rule describes could not be located; without it there is nothing for tsc to refuse and no test asserting the runtime drop.
rows.notes: Pending PO decision — the sink does not exist yet, which is the likely reason the type does not either. Re-check when the decision lands.

rows.rule: No error-telemetry SDK may be wired with its default configuration — auto-captured breadcrumbs, fetch/XHR payloads, console output, IP and session replay bypass the redactor and must be disabled explicitly in the adapter.
rows.statusBasis: There is no adapter and no SDK in the tree to fence, and no dependency-level ban (biome noRestrictedImports carries no telemetry package). The rule is a constraint on a future change.
rows.notes: Pending PO decision.

rows.rule: The physical tag activation code (generateTagActivationCode) is deliberately left unredacted by the client-error redactor.
rows.statusBasis: A declared accepted gap has no failing predicate. Note the interaction: redact-prefix-coverage.test.ts derives from generatePrefixedToken(...) literals, and this code is deliberately UNPREFIXED, so it is outside that fence's corpus by construction rather than by omission.
rows.notes: Stated as a known accepted gap, pending PO decision.

rows.rule: Dependencies in the module architecture must point inward: domain/ imports nothing outside itself, application/ depends only on domain/ and repository behavior, and only actions.ts/infrastructure/ may touch Next.js and the database.
rows.statusBasis: biome.json:98-105 (application override) restricts only next, next/cache, next/navigation, next/headers, server-only, @/lib/supabase/server — NOT @/db and NOT drizzle-orm, so the rule's "only actions.ts/infrastructure may touch the database" half is unfenced for src/modules/*/application/**. The domain override (:74-83) does ban both.
rows.notes: Independently derived the same uncovered clause the previous basis names. Second gap: scripts/application-fence-baseline.json holds exemptions=34, an exemption list whose members legitimately import restricted specifiers (check-application-fence.ts:24-39 ratchets it down only). check-dependency-direction.ts covers the between-module axis over src/modules/**/*.{ts,tsx} with an ALLOWED_EDGES list.

rows.rule: actions.ts must stay a thin Next.js controller: parse FormData, run the auth guard, build the input DTO, invoke the use-case, flush best-effort notifications, redirect — no business rules.
rows.statusBasis: scripts/check-action-line-budget.ts:79-97 fails only on LINE COUNT (existing > baseline+20, new > 150); logic that fits the slack or a 149-line new file passes, so 'no business rules' is measured by a size proxy. ACTIONS_GLOB at :40 is 'app/actions/*.ts' only — src/modules/*/actions.ts controllers are outside the fence entirely. lint:actions is in verify (package.json:79).
rows.notes: shape switched from ratchet to subset after the previous basis pointed at the uncovered directory; verified on :40, a line I had already opened. No other fence reads app/actions for business logic (check-dependency-direction.ts mentions it only in a comment, :59).

rows.rule: An action must never widen its authorization scope — a cross-org capability check that ignores the resource's own org is a security bug.
rows.statusBasis: scripts/check-confused-deputy.ts:172-180 fails only one syntactic shape — an action naming orgToken/senderOrgToken/receiverOrgToken (signature or formData) that gates with bare requireCapability; scripts/check-authz-scoping.ts is a report-only ratchet with 44 baselined offenders. 'Never widen authorization scope' is far broader than either predicate.
rows.notes: check-authz-scoping.ts:41-57 itself names two uncovered sibling rules (identity-only guard + caller-chosen pet id; role-not-allowed-for-the-effect).

rows.rule: A strangler migration must never drop side effects — audit_log rows, idempotency keys, and cascade closes are behavior and must be preserved byte-for-byte.
rows.statusBasis: scripts/check-audit-log-coverage.ts:342 catches only one of the three named side effects (an audit write disappearing from a non-baselined operator+mutating action, measured one hop into the use-case). Idempotency keys and cascade closes have no fence — rg 'idempotency' over scripts/ hits only seeds/backfills, no check-*. 'Byte-for-byte' payload preservation is measured by nothing.
rows.notes: the audit half is itself a ratchet with a 28-entry baseline

rows.rule: Coverage thresholds must be 90% branches on domain rules and 70-75% on the module/action layer.
rows.statusBasis: Reusing the refuter: vitest.config.ts:136-142 says these exact numbers 'were NEVER ENFORCED'; the live floors at :143-161 are business-rules 80, lib/** 55, app/actions 22, app/api 8, domain 88, src/modules 55 — no 90 and no 70-75. Coverage runs only under `pnpm test:coverage` (:116), which is absent from the verify chain. The named enforcer contradicts the rule it supposedly enforces.
rows.notes: docSays: 90 / 70-75. The live ratchet floors belong to a DIFFERENT rule, recorded by the refuter as a missing canon row (scope process).

rows.rule: lib/metrics/ (Pattern B) must not be imported from domain/ or application/ — it is infrastructure-adjacent and reads @/db directly.
rows.statusBasis: Reusing the refuter, confirmed against biome.json: the domain override (:74-83) restricts @/db, drizzle-orm, next, next/cache, next/navigation, next/headers, server-only and @/lib/supabase/server — NOT @/lib/metrics; the application override (:98-105) restricts six framework specifiers only. check-dependency-direction.ts:6-8 scopes itself to the BETWEEN-module axis.
rows.notes: A one-line biome paths entry would close it; nobody added one.

rows.rule: The per-offering campaign enrollment list and CSV are treated as operational data, not PII, and are exempt from k-anonymity suppression — only the geo-reach surface is k-suppressed.
rows.statusBasis: An EXEMPTION is not a checkable predicate here: no registry lists surfaces exempt from suppressSmallCells, so nothing would fail if the exemption were quietly widened to another surface. The branded SuppressedCells type (CANON-284) constrains only what DECLARES it.
rows.notes: Accepted by PO decision, 2026-07-12.

The second clause IS fenced, at :187-192: `Object.keys(resolved.updates).sort()` toEqual exactly checkAutomatically/enabled/fallbackToCacheTimeout/url, with :178-181 naming the reason ('A channel pinned in the app config would apply to EVERY build').
rows.notes: The previous basis capped this at PARTIAL saying the 'never declared in the app config' half 'was not found as an assertion'; :177-193 is that assertion, and it runs against the config the factory RESOLVES (built at :84-87 from app.json + app.config.ts), so an app.json-side channel is covered too. `updates.requestHeaders["expo-channel-name"]` is the only app-config route to a channel and the exact-key-set assertion excludes it.

rows.rule: The root package.json must pin packageManager to an exact pnpm version (pnpm@11.1.1) so the PO's machine, CI, and the EAS build worker all resolve native dependency paths with the same pnpm.
rows.statusBasis: release-config.test.ts:801-804 reads the ROOT package.json from disk and asserts `packageManager` matches /^pnpm@\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/ — the field's absence or a range pin (`pnpm@11`) fails. The rule's predicate is exactness of the pin, which the shape assertion covers.
rows.notes: docSays: pnpm@11.1.1; the fence deliberately pins the SHAPE, not the literal (comment at :798-800), so a deliberate upgrade is one edit. The specific version 11.1.1 is therefore not itself fenced — number left null on purpose.

rows.rule: CI workflow steps using pnpm/action-setup must not pass a version: input alongside the packageManager field, since the action compares them as raw strings and any mismatch fails the setup step in every job.
rows.statusBasis: release-config.test.ts:815-838 readdirs .github/workflows, walks every `pnpm/action-setup` step to the next list item collecting any `version:` input, asserts offenders toEqual([]) and adds a non-vacuity floor `stepsSeen > 0`. The `.endsWith(".yml")` filter covers 4 of 4 workflow files (rg --files .github/workflows: staging-health, mobile-export-nightly, codeql, ci — all .yml; the staging-facing nightlies moved to dim-interno on 2026-09-24 and are outside this test).
rows.notes: Latent filter risk only: a future .yaml workflow would escape the readdir filter. No .yaml exists at this SHA, so the corpus gate does not exclude any subject file (P20).
rows.numberKey: workflow steps carrying a version: input

rows.rule: apps/mobile/.gitignore must list /android/ and /ios/ (with the listing living inside apps/mobile/, not the repo root, since the fingerprint tool globs .gitignore from the Expo project root), and apps/mobile/.easignore must list the same two paths so a locally-run prebuild is never uploaded to EAS.
rows.statusBasis: Both halves are pinned by real assertions the v3 pass did not reach. apps/mobile/src/release/release-config.test.ts:849-854 reads apps/mobile/.gitignore FROM MOBILE_ROOT, splits it into trimmed non-comment lines, and expects the array to contain `/android/` and `/ios/` — the load-bearing location. :722-729 expects the root .easignore rule set to contain `apps/mobile/android/` and `apps/mobile/ios/`. Live files agree (apps/mobile/.gitignore:42-43, .easignore:188-189).
rows.notes: The v3 basis capped this at PARTIAL on the ground that release-config.test.ts:694-707 (the gitignore-parity and credential-path tests) does not cover the two entries — correct about :694-707, but it missed the two dedicated tests at :722-729 and :841-854, which I opened after reading the basis and which do exactly that. Mobile jest file; runs via pnpm verify -> verify:mobile -> `pnpm --filter mimar test` (package.json:78-79), which R8 buckets as test:verified. The basis is right that the rule's second path is loose: the .easignore is at the repo root, not apps/mobile/.easignore.

rows.rule: Every package a mobile config file imports by name must be declared in apps/mobile/package.json, checked by deriving standardized package names from every babel preset/plugin entry rather than hardcoding one name.
rows.statusBasis: release-config.test.ts:1400 is the line that FAILS when the rule is broken — `expect(named.filter((name) => !declared.has(name))).toEqual([])`, with a non-vacuity floor at :1406. The citation was `:931` until 2026-09-04; that line had drifted onto an unrelated assertion in the workflow-pin test, the icon work of that day shifted it onto a comment (`:1189`), which is what the canon-parity fence (b) reported, and the feature-graphic tests added later that day moved it once more; the Android-hardening tests (N1, 2026-09-24) moved it from :1326 to :1370. The test requires ../../babel.config.js, CALLS it, and derives package names from presets+plugins against apps/mobile/package.json's deps+devDeps — babel.config.js ONLY. The rule says 'every package a mobile config file imports by name': apps/mobile/metro.config.js:25 requires "expo/metro-config" and jest.config.js:54/:97 require "@react-native/jest-preset" and "jest-expo/jest-preset", none of them swept. The M17 location-permission pin (2026-09-25) moved it from :1370 to :1400.
rows.notes: Independently reached the judge's conclusion, and jest.config.js is a second uncovered config file the judge's note did not name. The derivation-not-hardcoding half of the rule is genuinely honoured (standardizeBabelName at :1208).

rows.rule: Every native dependency resolved into apps/mobile must satisfy the SDK's own bundledNativeModules.json pin, checked against the lockfile rather than declarations, so an undeclared auto-installed optional peer cannot drift silently.
rows.statusBasis: release-config.test.ts:1423-1425 reads expo/bundledNativeModules.json; :1439-1442 parses pnpm-lock.yaml's packages: section (the LOCKFILE, not declarations); :1547-1562 asserts every resolution of every bundled name satisfies the SDK pin, with a non-vacuity floor `checked >= MIN_BUNDLED_NAMES_CHECKED` at :1567. The two exempt web-owned names are re-pinned at :1570-1589. Citations re-anchored 2026-09-24: they had drifted onto the pnpm-pin test before N1 shifted the file again. Re-anchored again 2026-09-25 (+30) after the M17 location-permission pin.
rows.notes: The exemption (react, react-dom) is closed by a compensating assertion: whatever apps/mobile itself declares for an exempt name must equal the SDK pin (:1551), plus an exemption-list non-vacuity check (:1556-1558).

rows.rule: No .env* file may be read, created, or edited for mobile-emulator setup — the anon key must be taken from the running Supabase stack and passed inline.
rows.statusBasis: A PO rule about agent behaviour during a session, not a property of the tree. Nothing observes a read of a gitignored file. The related structural fact — .easignore must restate .env* (release-config.test.ts:705-707) — is a different rule (upload hygiene).
rows.notes: scripts/check-env-local.ts exists but is env:doctor (package.json:97), not in verify, and its subject is env completeness rather than this prohibition.

rows.rule: git status must be checked after any expo start or expo run:android and before any gate or commit, since either command can silently rewrite tracked config files.
rows.statusBasis: A session procedure. No hook, workflow step or fence asserts a clean tree after an expo command; CI never runs expo start at all.

rows.rule: A polling loop on a backgrounded mobile build/launch process must poll process liveness or an unconditional terminal marker, never match only for a success string.
rows.statusBasis: An agent-operations rule about how to wait on a child process; there is no committed launcher script whose polling shape a fence could inspect.

rows.rule: An OTA update must be subtractive only — after it, the app must not be able to do anything it could not do before.
rows.statusBasis: The policy's own framing is a judgement question. Its one MECHANISED consequence is the fingerprint runtimeVersion (CANON-449), which blocks native additions but says nothing about a JS-only capability addition.

rows.rule: Anything that changes the native runtime must never ship OTA (native module add/remove/upgrade, SDK/RN bump, config-plugin change, permissions/icon/splash, URL scheme/intent filters, build settings) — mechanically blocked by the runtimeVersion fingerprint policy.
rows.statusBasis: release-config.test.ts:166 asserts `resolved.runtimeVersion` toEqual { policy: "fingerprint" } on the config the app.config factory actually returns — a flip to appVersion fails. The rule names the fingerprint policy as ITS mechanism, and :771-783 / :785-805 / :841+ pin the two known fingerprint-reproducibility causes so the policy is not merely declared.
rows.notes: The per-change-kind list (native module, SDK bump, config plugin, permissions, icon/splash, intent filters) is enforced by EAS at publish time, not here; what the repo can fail on is the policy value and its reproducibility, both pinned.

rows.rule: Anything the store review would have needed to see (a new feature/surface, a data-collection change, a stated-purpose change, anything that changes a store questionnaire answer, anything worth announcing) must never ship OTA.
rows.statusBasis: The source itself says 'Not fenced by anything. This is the list that requires judgement.' Confirmed: no fence exists and none could without deciding what counts as a new surface.
rows.notes: The rule is explicitly self-declared as unenforceable; that is a design statement, not a gap draft 1 missed.

rows.rule: An OTA update must never assume a server contract not already deployed — the server must stay compatible with the oldest install still opening, since a released OTA cannot be recalled.
rows.statusBasis: No fence compares a mobile bundle's API expectations against the deployed server contract. @dim/contract is the shared type surface, and lint:contract keeps it installable — but nothing checks version skew between a published bundle and a deployed API.

rows.rule: An OTA fix must land in the tree normally first — through pnpm verify and pnpm test:verified and review — with no OTA-only code path and no patch that exists solely on a channel.
rows.statusBasis: A release procedure. Nothing can detect that a published bundle contains a commit absent from main; that comparison happens on EAS's servers and nothing in the repo reads it.

rows.rule: An OTA update must be proven JS-only via eas fingerprint:compare against the build being patched — never inferred from the diff.
rows.statusBasis: A manual command in a release runbook, not a gate. The related mechanism (runtimeVersion: fingerprint, CANON-449) makes a native-carrying update reach nobody, but nothing requires the operator to run the comparison first.

rows.rule: Every OTA hotfix must publish to the preview channel first, be installed and opened twice, and be confirmed before publishing to production.
rows.statusBasis: A manual release sequence on a physical device. The only mechanised part of the surrounding policy is the channel↔profile 1:1 mapping (CANON-439), which keeps `--channel preview` off production installs but does not order the two publishes.
rows.numberKey: required opens on the preview build

rows.rule: The next store release after any OTA hotfix must contain the same commit — an OTA that stays only on a channel across multiple releases is a fork.
rows.statusBasis: Requires comparing published channel contents to store build contents across time; neither side is readable from the repo, and no workflow reconciles them.

rows.rule: The pinned Node version must be >= 22.18.0 so packages/contract's raw .ts exports type-strip correctly for expo config.
rows.statusBasis: 22.18.0 occurs in scripts/check-node-version.ts only at :23, :32-36, :42 (the measurement table) and :273 (an error message) - all comment/string text. The predicates (:150-258) compare .nvmrc/.node-version/engines/workflows to EACH OTHER and :262 the running Node to engines; none compares any version against 22.18.0, and :197-209 explicitly permits a floor below the pin.
rows.notes: True at this SHA by declaration (pin 22.23.2, engines floor 22.23.0). v2 upgraded this to ENFORCED because the constraint is 'stated verbatim with the measurement behind it' - a comment stating a constraint is not a check. Lowering the pin below 22.18.0 fails nothing until a machine actually running that Node hits `expo config` inside verify:mobile (package.json:78).

rows.rule: The e2e Playwright job's Upload report step must run on always(), not failure(), because a timeout-minutes kill reports as cancelled and failure() is false for a cancelled job.
rows.statusBasis: .github/workflows/ci.yml:1046 `if: always()` on the Upload Playwright HTML report step IS the mechanism; editing it to `failure()` makes nothing exit non-zero. No fence reads workflow step conditions — check-scheduled-fence-refs only parses `schedule:`, `ref:`, `uses:` and `audited:`.
rows.notes: Self-executing declaration, true at this SHA; the reasoning is in the comment at :1041-1045. The v3 basis says outright 'The workflow line IS the mechanism' and still recorded ENFORCED.

rows.rule: e2e-nightly must check out the branch staging is deployed from (main), because a schedule trigger checks out only the default branch by default.
rows.statusBasis: e2e-nightly.yml moved to the private companion repository on 2026-09-24 with every staging-facing scheduled job (dim-interno:.github/workflows/e2e-nightly.yml). It checks out `repository: ignaciodelvalle/mimar`, `ref: main` — a literal held by hand. scripts/check-scheduled-fence-refs.ts scans only this repository's .github/workflows/ (scheduledWorkflows, :436-442), so nothing that can fail reads the file any more — the declaration IS the mechanism.
rows.notes: Was fenced by lint:sched-refs while the workflow lived in this repository. No private-enforcer convention exists in the canon, so the row is marked by what this repository can prove.

rows.rule: Playwright e2e is not part of pnpm verify; it runs only as CI's own job and nightly against staging.
rows.statusBasis: True on the live tree (the verify string at package.json:79 contains no playwright step; __tests__/db-reachability.ts:76 excludes e2e from the vitest walk) but neither direction can FAIL: adding `playwright test` to verify breaks nothing, and an e2e spec dropped into the vitest walk is skipped, not flagged.
rows.notes: No scripts/check-e2e-*.ts exists in the repo — confirmed by listing scripts/ and filtering for e2e/playwright.

rows.rule: pnpm test:e2e:smoke (public-smoke + crisis-owner-lost-flow specs) is expected before pushing feature ranges that touch public or lost-mode surfaces (/p/[token], /encontre, /perdidas, mark-lost, landing).
rows.statusBasis: package.json:133 defines test:e2e:smoke as exactly the two named specs, so the instrument exists and is correct — but 'expected before pushing' is a human obligation with no gate: nothing detects that a push touched a public/lost surface without it.
rows.notes: Not upgraded to PARTIAL: PARTIAL-by-wiring applies where the CHECK exists and only the wiring is missing; here the check itself (did this range touch those surfaces?) does not exist.

rows.rule: e2e tests must run against the built Next.js app (next build && next start), never the dev server.
rows.statusBasis: playwright.config.ts:116-119 is a webServer declaration — `pnpm build && pnpm start` (or `pnpm start` under NEXT_BUILT). Editing that command to `pnpm dev` fails nothing: no scripts/check-* fence and no test reads any playwright config (searched scripts/, __tests__/, .github/). The declaration IS the mechanism, so it is true at this SHA and unguarded.
rows.notes: self-executing declaration, true at this SHA. The basis holds ENFORCED on 'the config IS the mechanism for every local and CI run of this config' — the same shape as the CANON-002 calibration case (P10). ci.yml's e2e job builds and sets NEXT_BUILT, but no step exits 1 on the condition the rule names, so R2's CI exception does not apply.

rows.rule: e2e specs must never hardcode DB ids or tokens — real pet/org tokens are discovered at runtime from a live page (e.g. `/adoptar`, `/perdidas`), and the test skips cleanly when the seed has no matching fixture.
rows.statusBasis: The nearest fence, lint:uuid (scripts/check-uuid-literals.ts), scopes itself to app/, components/, lib/, src/ (:13) and explicitly exempts tests and fixtures (:14-16) — so e2e/ is outside its corpus twice over. Nothing scans e2e specs for literal tokens or ids.
rows.notes: Note the tension with CANON-479, which forbids skipping on a seeded fixture; the README's own 'skips cleanly' clause is the one CANON-468/469/470 narrow to environment-branching.

rows.rule: chapas.spec.ts must clean up its own lote via deleteTagsByLotePrefix against the local DB only, since the product has no "delete a chapa" flow.
rows.statusBasis: A per-spec obligation with no fence: nothing asserts chapas.spec.ts calls the cleanup helper, and nothing prevents the helper being pointed at a non-local target. There is no scripts/check-e2e-*.ts in the repo at all.

rows.rule: api-v1-auth-refusals.spec.ts must sign in nowhere — every case must be a refusal so the suite never spends the auth_login_email budget.
rows.statusBasis: A property of one spec's contents. No fence asserts the absence of a loginAs call in that file, and the rate-limit budget it protects is only observable as a downstream flake.

rows.rule: The demo/ narrated recording scripts must not be run as part of a normal e2e pass.
rows.statusBasis: playwright.config.ts:63 `testIgnore: ["demo/**", "perf/**"]` is a config declaration; :57-62 says four configs carry it and asks the reader to "keep them in sync", recording that local3000 was missed in a previous pass. No fence compares the configs and no test reads them, so deleting the line fails nothing directly.
rows.notes: self-executing declaration, true at this SHA. The basis reaches ENFORCED from the same two config lines while its own notes concede 'Nothing fences that synchronisation' — that concession is the verdict under R2. Removing the line would eventually blow globalTimeout (:82) in CI, but that is a consequence of run length, not a check of this predicate.

rows.rule: New spec files under e2e/ (outside demo/ and perf/) automatically join the nightly staging pass — no workflow file change is needed.
rows.statusBasis: playwright.staging.config.ts:120-121 declares testDir './e2e' + testIgnore ['demo/**','perf/**'] and dim-interno:.github/workflows/e2e-nightly.yml runs that config on cron (moved to the private companion repository on 2026-09-24 with every staging-facing scheduled job). The auto-inclusion IS the declaration; widening testIgnore fails nothing. No fence reads either file (rg over scripts/, __tests__/ = 0; check-scheduled-fence-refs.ts has no testDir/testIgnore subject).
rows.notes: self-executing declaration, true at this SHA; the previous basis reaches the same description ('the config IS the mechanism') but rated it ENFORCED

rows.rule: CI's fresh-seed DB must be the judge of a passing suite, never a developer's laptop DB, which accumulates state that makes local runs unreliable.
rows.statusBasis: A rule about which verdict a human should believe. Nothing can fail on it — a green local full-suite run is indistinguishable from any other, and no gate refuses a locally-produced e2e report as evidence.
rows.notes: Structurally supported (CI runs `pnpm exec supabase start` + bootstrap before the e2e job, ci.yml:1034 area) but that supports the rule rather than enforcing it.

rows.rule: A fixture-gated check must branch on the ENVIRONMENT, never on the data — test.skip(rowsFound === 0, ...) is disallowed; use the e2e/_seed-profile.ts seed profile instead.
rows.statusBasis: __tests__/e2e-seed-profile.test.ts:13-68 only exercises resolveSeedProfile/seedFixtureVerdict on literal args; nothing scans e2e/*.spec.ts. The banned shape is live and unfenced: e2e/print-surfaces.spec.ts:53,76,87 test.skip((await petLink.count()) === 0, ...) and e2e/race-battery.spec.ts:74 — verbatim the construct the rule disallows.
rows.notes: v3 reached the same gap ('nothing scans e2e/*.spec.ts for the BANNED shape') but capped at PARTIAL. R7's second branch: the rule's predicate IS adoption of the seed profile, so the helper's own test proves nothing about callers and no fence mandates the single door.

rows.rule: Under the bootstrap seed profile (CI default), a missing fixture must SKIP with a reason naming the coverage hole.
rows.statusBasis: __tests__/e2e-seed-profile.test.ts:59-68 asserts seedFixtureVerdict(0, ..., 'bootstrap') returns verdict 'skip' with a reason containing 'NO COVERAGE' — the helper's behaviour is genuinely pinned. No caller is forced through it: e2e/print-surfaces.spec.ts:53,76,87 and e2e/race-battery.spec.ts:74 gate on data with no profile at all.
rows.notes: R7 first branch — the rule states the mechanism's BEHAVIOUR, adoption implied, so PARTIAL not ENFORCED. v3 called this ENFORCED while calling the sibling CANON-479 adoption-unfenced on the same file; the gap is the same one. The bootstrap case pins only the 'NO COVERAGE' marker — the fixture/unmeasured naming is pinned on the 'full' branch (:46-53), not here.

rows.rule: Under the full seed profile (staging/nightly), a missing fixture must FAIL.
rows.statusBasis: __tests__/e2e-seed-profile.test.ts:41-53 asserts seedFixtureVerdict(0, ..., 'full').verdict === 'fail' and that the reason names both the fixture ('/perdidas') and what went unmeasured ('the axe audit'). Callers escape: e2e/print-surfaces.spec.ts:53,76,87 skip on (await petLink.count()) === 0 regardless of profile, so under 'full' a missing fixture there still skips instead of failing.
rows.notes: Helper behaviour fully pinned in both directions (:36-39 runs when present); the rule's effect on the corpus is not. Same R7 first-branch reasoning as CANON-469.

rows.rule: e2e assertions must be deterministic: web-first assertions only, no arbitrary sleep, no reliance on Date.now() or randomness.
rows.statusBasis: No fence scans e2e specs for waitForTimeout, Date.now() or Math.random(). biome's rules apply to the repo but none of them bans these; there is no scripts/check-e2e-*.ts.
rows.notes: A cheap, high-value fence candidate: the three banned shapes are all grep-able literals in a bounded corpus.

rows.rule: loginAs must call resetAuthLoginRateLimits() before every real sign-in; any spec with its own private login must do the same.
rows.statusBasis: The helper exists (e2e/demo/_db-cleanup.ts, used by e2e/demo/_helpers.ts) but nothing enforces the 'any spec with its own private login' clause: exactly one spec calls it directly today (e2e/owner-ia-p6.spec.ts), and a new private login would be caught only as a rate-limit flake.

rows.rule: The anonymous denuncia rate limit is 1/min per IP; e2e specs must pass a unique uniqueIp() per walk to avoid tripping it.
rows.statusBasis: No fence requires a uniqueIp() argument at a denuncia call site in e2e specs. The limit itself lives in the product's rate-limit config; the spec-side obligation has no mechanism.
rows.notes: number carried from the doc; the live rate-limit constant was NOT re-read in this pass, so treat 1/min as docSays until confirmed against lib/rate-limit.ts.
rows.numberKey: anonymous denuncia writes per minute per IP

rows.rule: Against a staging target, uniqueIp() is not honoured (Vercel overwrites x-real-ip); protection must instead be structural — sign in once per account per worker and space out repeated anonymous writes.
rows.statusBasis: A target-dependent authoring rule. Nothing distinguishes a local-only technique used against staging; the failure appears as a nightly red, which is the symptom the rule exists to explain rather than a fence.

rows.rule: e2e specs must never assert a 404 by HTTP status — assert the branded-not-found surface (testid) instead, since a streaming route can answer 200 with a denied page after headers already went out.
rows.statusBasis: __tests__/e2e-page-identity.test.ts:58-106 pins NOT_FOUND_HEADING against every app/**/not-found.tsx and that BrandedNotFound carries the testid (:102-104); no line inspects e2e spec source for a status-404 assertion. Live counterexamples pass green: e2e/api-v1-public-contract.spec.ts:148 expect(res.status()).toBe(404), e2e/cross-tenant-isolation.spec.ts:126 toContain(status) over [200,404].
rows.notes: The v3 basis rests on the instrument being fenced. The rule's predicate is a PROHIBITION on spec authors, not the instrument's behaviour, so R7's second branch applies: the only walker over the e2e corpus is e2e-sign-in-route.test.ts:45, and it bans the /login literal.

rows.rule: e2e specs must never wait on a post-action URL — assert the outcome the mutation produces, since useActionRedirect's window.location.assign drops often enough to matter.
rows.statusBasis: No fence scans e2e specs for waitForURL. lint:action-redirect (scripts/check-action-redirect.ts, in verify) governs the PRODUCT side — how server actions redirect — not how a spec waits on one.

rows.rule: e2e dates must be computed as ART-local via Intl.DateTimeFormat with America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires, never via toISOString(), because the server rejects future dates in Argentina time.
rows.statusBasis: lint:timezone (scripts/check-timezone-*.ts) is in the verify chain but its corpus is product source, not e2e/. Nothing scans specs for toISOString() used as a date input.
rows.notes: Same family as CANON-202/203 (host clock vs the authoritative clock) and equally unfenced; a single 'clock discipline' fence could cover all three corpora.

rows.rule: e2e specs must gate every DOM read behind an auto-retrying expect() first — Locator.count() does not auto-retry and must never be the sole basis for a test.skip().
rows.statusBasis: No fence scans e2e specs for `.count()` feeding a test.skip. This is the same banned shape as CANON-468's second clause and is unfenced for the same reason: no scripts/check-e2e-*.ts exists.

rows.rule: e2e skips must be reserved for genuine ENVIRONMENTAL conditions, never for a fixture the repo's own seed guarantees — a guaranteed fixture must be asserted, so a missing one turns red.
rows.statusBasis: __tests__/e2e-seed-profile.test.ts:35-68 judges only the helper's return values on literal arguments. e2e/print-surfaces.spec.ts:53 skips with 'No adoptable pets seeded — no credential to print.' — a fixture the repo's own seed provides — and nothing turns red; no fence reads e2e spec source for skip predicates.
rows.notes: v3 named the same adoption gap and capped at PARTIAL. The rule's predicate is a directive to spec authors ('skips are for environmental conditions; if the seed guarantees it, ASSERT it'), i.e. adoption proper → R7 second branch, and a live violating skip exists. Blind calibration dissent (1 of 18 sampled rows): the blind reader derived PARTIAL (adoption-unfenced) where v4 says UNENFORCED. v4's verdict stands — the rule's predicate is adoption itself and no production path is forced through the helper.

rows.rule: Every remaining e2e skip must print its reason, since CI's e2e job uses --reporter=list,github,html and only "list" surfaces skip reasons in the job log.
rows.statusBasis: .github/workflows/ci.yml:1034 `pnpm e2e --reporter=list,github,html` is a config string and checks nothing about skips. The rule's predicate is adoption ('every remaining skip prints its reason') and only the helper is pinned: __tests__/e2e-seed-profile.test.ts:66-67 asserts the seed-profile outcome carries a reason, while each spec is free to call test.skip with an empty string (e2e/print-surfaces.spec.ts:185 passes "" on its non-skip branch).
rows.notes: No scripts/check-*.ts scans e2e/ for skips without a reason. The v3 basis called the reporter half 'the enforced half', but a reporter flag is R2 config: with the obligation half unfenced and the config half not an enforcer at all, there is no covered part left to make this PARTIAL.

rows.rule: Multi-step wizard specs must walk every step and click the actual last-step submit button, never an earlier step's button of the same name.
rows.statusBasis: An authoring rule about locator choice inside a spec. No fence models wizard step structure, and the failure mode it prevents (a wait on an element that step never renders) surfaces only as a timeout.

rows.rule: playwright.config.ts must set actionTimeout: 15s so an unbounded Playwright action fails legibly instead of silently eating the whole test budget.
rows.statusBasis: playwright.config.ts:103 `actionTimeout: 15_000` (reason at :92) is a value the runner consumes; nothing can FAIL on it being edited to 0. rg over scripts/ and __tests__/ for 'playwright.config' returns zero — no fence or test pins it. The previous basis says the same thing ('the config line IS the mechanism'), which is the P10/CANON-002 test for a self-executing declaration.
rows.notes: self-executing declaration, true at this SHA (15_000 live)

rows.rule: Append new locked-in design decisions worth preserving across sessions to AGENTS.md.
rows.statusBasis: No enforcer found: no scripts/check-*.ts, no vitest/jest fence, no biome override, no CI step and no DB constraint has this rule's subject as its predicate. It is a working norm applied by hand.

rows.rule: Any change that adds a new event type or modifies the schema requires a spec in docs/superpowers/specs/ written and iterated before the code PR is opened, with the spec link in the PR description.

rows.rule: Writes to the database from `app/**` go ONLY through a `src/modules/<domain>` use case called from `actions.ts`; page-level READS from `app/**` straight through Drizzle are tolerated under a shrink-only baseline; and no `app/**` file beyond the one already recorded may insert into the `petEvents` spine.

rows.rule: The shared pet-profile icon vocabulary may not map a concept to a bare geometric placeholder, and no two concept keys may wear the same glyph without a declared alias.
rows.statusBasis: scripts/check-mobile-icon-vocabulary.ts parses PET_PROFILE_ICONS out of packages/contract/src/icons/pet-profile-icons.ts and applies three rules through the exported `evaluate(source)`. Rule A (:231) fails any value in PLACEHOLDER_GLYPHS (Circle, Square, Box, Dot, Minus, Slash, HelpCircle, CircleDashed, SquareDashed) with no baseline; Rule B (:253) fails any glyph used by more than one key unless the key set matches a DECLARED_ALIASES entry exactly, and :266 fails the reverse — a declared alias the table no longer duplicates; Rule C (:200-227) fails an unreadable source (one violation, not two), a parse of zero, a count below MIN_ENTRIES, or any key→glyph pair that differs from the pinned PINNED_TABLE pair list, naming the rows added and removed. Exit 1 at :286 on any violation. __tests__/check-mobile-icon-vocabulary.test.ts exercises all four shapes against fixtures, including the real pre-4fa613500 table. components/Icon.test.tsx closes the other side by asserting every table key exists in the web ICON_MAP and maps to the SAME component by reference. package.json lint:mobile-icons is in the verify chain and .github/workflows/ci.yml runs it in the `check` job, so CI blocks a merge on it too (check-ci-lint-parity enforces that pairing).
rows.notes: Written 2026-09-03 after `embarazo: "Baby"` and `fallecimiento: "Circle"` both shipped to a store build. apps/mobile/src/ui/Icon.test.tsx had fenced this table since 2026-09-01 and was GREEN on both, because it only asserts that each value resolves to a real lucide-react-native export — a question that cannot detect a glyph which resolves and means nothing. The three rules here are the mechanically decidable part; semantic correctness is NOT automatable, and Rule C's pin is what makes a change to the table visible in review instead of quiet. Reworked the same day after review: the pin was a COUNT, which reports that something moved and not what, so a same-count glyph swap read as clean — it is now a pair list whose failure message shows `- embarazo:CalendarHeart / + embarazo:Baby` inside the fence file itself. The header's claim that both mechanical rules had each caught a real defect was also corrected: Rule A caught one, Rule B has caught nothing that shipped and is a forward guard. This fence is also the first that scans anything outside the root Next.js tree: the six web design fences (lint:icons, lint:buttons, lint:states, lint:empty-states, lint:screens, lint:copy-contract) all resolve their globs against app/ and components/ and none of them includes apps/mobile, so the Expo client had no design fence at all before this one.

rows.rule: The native amend form may offer a fact row only when the server's curated projection renders that (event type, field) pair VERBATIM and the value is free text; every formatted or date-pushed row is read-only on the phone.
rows.statusBasis: The fence parses lib/events/events.ts's eventPayloadDetails switch into (arm, label, field, transformed, dated) rows and apps/mobile/src/pets/event-detail-view-model.ts's PASS_THROUGH_FACTS into (type, field) pairs, then offends when any allowlisted pair is rendered through a transform or pushDate (:246), or names a type outside AMENDABLE_EVENT_TYPES where no form can reach it (:250). It is a SUBSET check on purpose — the phone being more conservative than the projection must not go red. Non-vacuity at :284-297 pins arms >= 8, rows >= 28, pass-through >= 20, transformed >= 5, dated >= 3, phone types >= 5 and pairs >= 13, all measured against the real corpus (10/34/24/6/4 and 6/16) on 2026-09-07. :300 re-asserts the three rows the defect was reported on; :315 offends on a key pushed twice when either push is formatted; :329 refuses an allowlist it cannot actually parse (zero-field entry, key-count mismatch, quoted-string-count mismatch); :347 proves it recognises a transform newly added to an allowlisted key.
rows.notes: Written 2026-09-07 as the containment for A2-alta-asentar-02: the amend form pre-filled the FORMATTED es-AR value and posted the edited text as the raw payload value, so a date correction wrote '15/03/2026' into next_due_at and 12/04/2026 was parsed US-style as 4 December — silently wrong on an APPEND-ONLY spine, where only another correction can sit on top and nothing marks the value as wrong. The rule is an ALLOWLIST so a new event type, a new fact key or a changed rendering lands OUTSIDE it and is refused by default. Review found the first draft's rule ('renders verbatim') necessary but not sufficient: to_country and origin_country are ISO-3166 codes rendered verbatim, so the phone drew a text box reading 'AR' that an owner would helpfully correct to 'Argentina' — which then fails the toCountry === 'AR' gate in refresh-pet-cache-after-amendment.ts and nulls pets.localityId. The rule is now verbatim AND free text. The proper fix (rawValue on EventFactV1, enum rows as a Choice, per-field schema validation) is server-first and not OTA-able over the installed build.

rows.rule: The native amend form may not post a null for a fact the spine declares non-nullable; the phone's NON_NULLABLE_FACTS list must agree with the real payload schemas in both directions.
rows.statusBasis: buildAmendChanges emits a change per edited box and used to emit value: null for an emptied one; nothing re-validates the target payload after an amendment, so clearing 'Vacuna' wrote null into a required field and the projection then dropped the row. NON_NULLABLE_FACTS names the spine-required keys and the change is dropped rather than posted, with clearedRequiredFact/amendRequiredFactMessage making the refusal visible. Because that list is a second cache of a server fact, the fence runs a REAL base payload through the REAL PayloadSchemas and flips one allowlisted field to null at a time (:492), judging both directions — a key the phone calls required that the spine accepts as null, and a key the phone omits that the spine refuses. :481 first proves every base payload it judges against is itself valid, and :489 floors BASE_PAYLOADS at 8, :523 floors probed fields at 13.
rows.notes: Written 2026-09-07 alongside CANON-528. The allowlist governs which ROWS may be edited and never which VALUES may be written, which is how the null case survived the first draft; this row closes the value half. The two-direction check is the point — a one-direction fence would let the phone quietly become more permissive than the spine as schemas change.
rows.numberKey: minimum allowlisted fields probed against the spine

rows.rule: The native app may not fall silently behind the owner's web: every owner-guarded server action must reach a use-case the v1 surface also reaches, every receipt fact the web shows must be obtainable from a v1 read, the three kind vocabularies (contract, phone, router) must agree, and every deliberate divergence must be declared with a reason and what would close it.
rows.statusBasis: scripts/check-owner-surface-parity.ts derives both sides at run time and enumerates nothing: the owner guards come from the `require…PetAccess|PetByToken|TitularAccess` exports of lib/infra/pet-access.ts + lib/infra/pets.ts; the web set is every exported async function in a "use server" file under app/actions, app/(app)/mis-mascotas and src/modules whose body CALLS one of those guards; the app set is every src/modules/**/application/** use-case that a file under app/api/v1 imports and names, with relative (`./application/x`) and absolute (`@/src/modules/…`) specifiers resolved to one id. findDivergences (:609-663) fails an action whose called use-case no v1 route reaches (`write:`), an action with no use-case at all (`unjoined:`), and a result field the action reads that no v1 file reads and no packages/contract/src/api DTO declares (`read:`). vocabularyFailures (:665-693) parses `kind: z.literal` from record-event.ts, WRITABLE_KINDS (+RECORD_KINDS spread) from the phone's view-model and EVENT_TYPE_OF_KIND from writers.ts and fails any set difference, naming the kinds. declarationFailures (:695-721) fails an undeclared divergence, a declaration missing `reason` or `closes`, and a stale declaration. vacuityFailures (:567-607) fails when any scan is under its floor (guards 3, use-server files 40, owner actions 30, joined actions 15, v1 use-cases 20, kinds 12, DTO keys 200 — measured 4/82/44/34/95/18/359 on 2026-09-09) or a vocabulary source cannot be parsed. Exit 1 at :771. __tests__/check-owner-surface-parity.test.ts mutates the live inputs one thing at a time: dropping `bite` from the phone is named as `in contract only: bite`; renaming WRITABLE_KINDS fails the floor and reports no disagreement; a synthetic action with an unreached use-case, a synthetic receipt field, an emptied v1 set, an emptied guard set, a hollow declaration, a stale declaration and an undeclared finding are each named. package.json lint:owner-parity is in the verify chain and .github/workflows/ci.yml runs it in the `check` job (lint:ci-parity holds the pairing).
rows.notes: Written 2026-09-09, the day the app reached the eighteenth owner kind (post_adoption_checkin) and the PO asked for parity to be MEASURED before the next native build rather than believed from prose. The first run found 12 divergences, all declared in DECLARED_DIVERGENCES with reason + closure and reported to the PO: the mordedura case code no v1 read carries (the one gap the router's own header already named), the tattoo asiento the '18 of 18' never counted, species correction, the vaccine-reminder pair, the three rehome titular actions, the physical-tag interest toggle, the web-only 'primeros pasos' dismissal, and two that are parity in fact but not in the one-hop join (recordMoveAction reaches recordMovementWriter through recordJurisdictionMove; disclosureKeyRequiresTitular is a guard-chooser, not a door). Deliberately NOT decided here: the reverse direction (a v1 door the web lacks), the field-for-field shape of each kind's input (the contract's job), and whether a v1 route's guard is as wide as the web's (lint:authz). The join is one hop deep by design — a use-case reached through another use-case is declared, not inferred.

rows.rule: Every runtime load of maplibre-gl must go through lib/ui/maplibre-loader.ts, which calls setWorkerUrl() once before any Map is constructed; the worker and its shared chunk are generated into public/maplibre/ by prebuild/predev and are never committed.
rows.statusBasis: check-maplibre-worker.ts scans app/components/lib/src with comments stripped and fails on any import("maplibre-gl") outside the loader; it also fails when package.json loses the prebuild/predev hooks, when MAPLIBRE_WORKER_URL and the copy destination disagree, when the installed worker stops importing ./maplibre-gl-shared.mjs, and when a served copy differs from node_modules. A non-vacuity check fails if the scan cannot even see the loader's own import. lint:maplibre-worker is in verify (package.json) and in ci.yml; lint:ci-parity keeps the two in step.
rows.notes: MEASURED, not stylistic. maplibre-gl 6 resolves its worker at runtime through new URL('./maplibre-gl-worker.mjs', import.meta.url) — a form no bundler detects statically, so webpack emits no asset: after a clean pnpm build, `find .next -iname "*worker*"` returned nothing. The fetch does not 404; Next answers the app's own HTML with a 200, the worker executes HTML as JavaScript and dies silently, and the map renders an empty canvas with every layer and source registered and zero features in all of them — no console output, no failed request, no CSP violation. It cost a day of ruling out the database, WebGL2, the load handler, legacy expressions and the CSP. The A/B on one tree: canvas PNG 141099 bytes with the worker present, 82981 with the same file taken away. The e2e spec that covered this page only asserted the canvas was VISIBLE, which it was, which is why the blank map survived months of green.

rows.rule: No tracked file may carry a secret-shaped credential — a postgres URL with an inline password, a non-demo service_role JWT or sb_secret key, a live Stripe/Resend/AWS key, a private key block, a literal password or high-entropy *_SECRET/*_PASSWORD/*_TOKEN/*_API_KEY assignment in config or docs, or the seeded demo password outside the code that logs the demo accounts in; the local stack's published demo values are exempt by exact value, and every other exception is a reasoned one-kind-one-path ALLOWLIST entry that fails once it matches nothing.
rows.statusBasis: scripts/check-secrets.ts:473-520 runs findSecrets (:332-341, every SCANNER over every line) on every `git ls-files` path except binaries and files over 2 MiB, applies the allowlist (:428-446) and exits 1 on any unallowlisted finding (file:line + kind, never the value) and on any allowlist entry that matched nothing; :474-479 fails a zero-file listing instead of passing it. The non-vacuity floor is __tests__/check-secrets.test.ts:79-97 — every SECRET_KINDS member must fire on a synthetic sample and a new kind without one fails — and :293-299 self-scans the fence and its test. package.json:80 lint:secrets is in the verify chain and .github/workflows/ci.yml runs it in its own step (lint:ci-parity holds the pairing).
rows.notes: Scope is tracked files at HEAD by design (header :63-65): untracked/ignored files such as .env.local are where secrets belong, and history is not scanned — a value already published is not unpublished by this fence, which is why the failure message says to rotate. Closes the 'no secrets' half of CANON-022 for the tree, not its 'clean history' half. L-24 in dim-interno:docs/plans/PENDIENTES.md; env_secret_assignment was added 2026-09-18 after a security review found a pasted CRON_SECRET matched nothing.

rows.rule: A replay of a projection that reads an amendable event type (replayPetWeight, replayPetPregnancy, replayPetJurisdiction) must be handed a stream that went through overlayAmendments and whose fetch includes event_amended; only overlayAmendments may mint the AmendmentOverlaid brand — enforced against ANY CAST THAT NAMES THE BRAND (including one a formatter wraps across lines) and against the unnamed forgery: a replayPet* call's argument list is split on top-level commas only (nested calls/objects/arrays and quoted/template-literal text are skipped whole, not treated as argument boundaries), and any single argument that — once unwrapped of parens enclosing it whole — ends in a top-level `as any`/`as never` is a forgery, regardless of what nested structure it contains (`pick(events, "x") as any` and `(raw as any)` both fail; `{ meta: raw as any }` does not, because the cast there is inside an object the argument merely contains, not applied to the argument itself). Every other raw pet_events payload reader (Drizzle petEvents.payload or a raw-SQL alias such as med.payload->>) in a file naming an amendable type must overlay, use the SQL twin, or be classified in the fence (via / other-type / raw-by-design / debt), and a new unclassified reader fails; a file carrying BOTH forms must satisfy each form's own coverage mechanism independently.
rows.statusBasis: scripts/check-amendment-overlay.ts derives the amendable replays from AMENDABLE_EVENT_TYPES and the lib/projections sources (never a copied list). payloadReadForms (:323) recognises both the Drizzle column and a raw-SQL alias read in a file naming pet_events as an ARRAY, not a single value, so a file carrying both forms is checked on both independently — closing a gap where `overlayAmendments(` called for an UNRELATED Drizzle read used to blanket-exempt a raw alias read the fence never checked (owner-dashboard.ts's fetchOngoingMedications read drug_name raw this way; fixed same review, owner-dashboard.ts now a KNOWN_READERS anchor). brandForgers (:513) fails any cast that names the brand outside lib/infra/amendment.ts, tests included, now matching across lines (a biome-wrapped cast used to be invisible), PLUS every replayPet* call findForgedCastCalls (:499) flags via splitTopLevelArgs (:402, a depth-aware comma splitter over ()[]{} that skips quoted/template strings whole) and isForgedCastArgument (:484, true when a single argument, unwrapped of enclosing parens, ends in a top-level `as any`/`as never`). This replaced a single regex (`/(?:^|,)\s*[^,()]*\bas\s+(?:any|never)\b/` applied to the whole raw argument-list text) a fresh-context review found BOTH too narrow — `[^,()]*` cannot cross a nested call's parens, so `replayPetWeight(pick(events, "x") as any)` was invisible to it — AND too broad — a comma inside a nested call or object was read as an argument boundary, so `replayPetWeight(events, { filter: buildFilter(a, b), meta: raw as any })` was flagged for a cast that never touched the whole argument. __tests__/check-amendment-overlay.test.ts pins both reviewer cases plus a multi-line biome-wrapped cast, a legit overlayAmendments(raw) call, and a string literal containing ", x as any" that must not be mistaken for code. checkReplayReader fails a replay caller without overlayAmendments or whose type-narrowed fetch omits event_amended, and refuses to allowlist it; checkPayloadReader fails an unclassified reader, a 'via' entry whose token left the file, and an entry for a file that now overlays; checkScan floors the scan at 40 readers and eight known readers (two alias-form anchors, one file-vs-form anchor) and fails entries for missing files. The type side is AmendmentOverlaid (lib/projections/types.ts:31). events-repository.test.ts pins A08-G1/G2 against the real DB.
rows.notes: Written 2026-09-22 for T3-A1 (A08-G1..G4, A05-7), widened the same day after a fresh security review (alias form, brand-cast rule), widened again the same day after a SECOND fresh review (file-vs-form exemption gap, multi-line/unnamed brand casts), and the unnamed-forgery check rewritten the same day after a THIRD fresh-context review found its regex both too narrow and too broad (see statusBasis) — replaced with the depth-aware splitTopLevelArgs/isForgedCastArgument pair, with its own test file added (T3-R2). The ALLOWLIST carries 7 'debt' entries — real raw reads of amendable payloads left for follow-up (sighting notes in the lost surfaces, medication and sterilization displays, movement counts). Known classes OUTSIDE the model: (1) insert-time copy columns such as pet_events.proxima_dosis_at (read by lib/analytics/org-dashboard.ts) never follow a correction and are not payload reads, so the fence cannot see them; (2) checkPayloadReader is per-file-and-form, not per individual read site — a file with two raw alias reads of the same amendable type, one wrapped in amendedPayloadText and one not, passes on the strength of the first; closing that needs data-flow analysis this text-based fence does not attempt.
