rows.statusBasis: scripts/check-dispute-lock-predicate.ts fails on (a) a drizzle eq/ne/inArray/notInArray against custodyDisputes.status naming open without escalated, (b) a <something>dispute.status ===/!== "open" comparison, (c) a drizzle sql`` template predicating on status inside the custodyDisputes pgTable block — the shape the partial indexes themselves are written in, and the one the original bug had — and (d) a custody_disputes SQL statement predicating on open alone via =, !=, <>, in or not in, across db/*.sql and migrations >= 0242, with dollar-quoted bodies kept whole. Scans app, db, lib, src and scripts. Two vacuity guards: the run fails if it opened no files, and if it sees fewer than 15 predicate call sites outside db/schema.ts and the fence itself. Wired via lint:dispute-lock inside `verify` and as its own CI step. The behavioural half is __tests__/custody-dispute-escalated-keeps-lock.test.ts (13 tests) plus __tests__/custody-dispute-action-revalidation.test.ts (4), each mutation-proven.
rows.notes: PO decision 2A, 2026-09-22. Migration 0235 made escalated representable and deliberately left every reader keyed on open, which made writing the value a silent release of the lock; migration 0242 widened the custody_disputes_one_open_per_pet and custody_disputes_juris_open_idx partial indexes, and this change moved the thirteen TypeScript readers onto disputeHoldsCustodyLock() / isInDisputeStatus(). Migrations below 0242 are immutable history and fall outside the fence's scan window by construction. Hardened after a security review on the same day: db/** was originally outside the scan globs (so the file the bug came from was never checked for violations), the non-vacuity floor was satisfiable with zero call sites, and the SQL rule understood neither negated operators nor dollar-quoted bodies.

rows.rule: Every field of a useActionState form that React 19 does not control must survive the automatic reset that follows a rejected action: a text input/textarea is genuinely React-controlled (value+onChange) or seeds from useKeptFields's kept(); a <select> is keyed off kept() (or off plain state when it never round-trips through the action), never off live state alone; a checkbox/radio seeds its defaultChecked from useKeptFields's keptChecked(), OR from plain live state PAIRED WITH BOTH a changing key and an onChange (proof the expression tracks what was actually clicked, not a value fixed once at mount) — checked= (controlled) is NEVER safe on its own for a checkbox/radio, and neither is a defaultChecked keyed only for React's ordinary list-key requirement with no onChange; anything this fence cannot see is already safe is allowlisted with a written reason.
rows.statusBasis: scripts/check-kept-fields-adoption.ts walks every useActionState file field by field (not file-wide, so a form that adopts the hook and misses one select still fails) and flags an unsafe select/checkbox/radio/text that neither seeds from kept()/keptChecked() nor carries an allowlist reason. Wired as lint:kept-fields inside `verify` and as its own CI step; scripts/check-kept-fields-adoption.test.ts covers the shapes. Since batch 3, detectLocalTextWrappers() extends scanning through single-level local field-wrapper components (a helper that forwards a bare name={name} to a recognized primitive). Since batch 4: the checkbox/radio check no longer only flags checked= (controlled) — an uncontrolled defaultChecked that is not itself keptChecked(...), and not a plain-state defaultChecked paired with BOTH a changing key and an onChange (mirroring the <select> defaultValue+key exception, but requiring onChange too since a checkbox/radio's defaultChecked resyncs on react-dom's UPDATE path regardless of remounts — a key alone, the ordinary React list-key every list-rendered checkbox carries, proves nothing; FinalizeAdoptionForm.tsx's __appChoice/useFosterShortcut are the genuinely-safe key+onChange shape, AgendaRuleForm.tsx's original key-only defaultChecked was the bug this refinement re-catches after a first version missed it) — is flagged, since a native form.reset() restores checked to whatever was true at mount otherwise; and the file-level useActionState( detection now also matches useActionState<StateType, PayloadType>(, which the old regex missed entirely (found via ShareLibretaSheet.tsx, previously invisible to this fence in full). A fresh-context review of batches 3-4 then found and closed four more gaps: the select/checkbox key= check required only that a key EXIST, not that it CHANGE (a bare key={value} or an ordinary per-item list key like key={d.value} satisfied it; now the key expression itself must be a template literal — a backtick or ${ — the same spelling every hand-verified fix already used); a local wrapper detected only for its text-ish passthrough could still be called with checked=/defaultChecked= and fall through to the TEXT rule's controlled check, which a checkbox's own submitted value= satisfies just as well as a text field's does (latent, closed by testing for checked=/defaultChecked= ahead of tagName/type=); attrExpr's [^}]* regex truncated at the FIRST }, wrong for any expression containing one before its own close (a template literal's ${...}, an object literal) — brace- and quote-balanced now, same technique as readOpeningTag; and the allowlist marker exempted a file from every check above ENTIRELY and forever, uncounted by anything — a second ratchet, ALLOWLISTED_BASELINE (currently 7), now fails the same way a new unsafe form does if a marker is added without a deliberate, reviewed bump. Also that review: kept(name) could not distinguish 'nothing submitted yet' from 'submitted, and this field was blank', so the kept(name) || fallback pattern every call site used resurrected the fallback over a field someone had deliberately CLEARED — kept now takes the fallback as a second, explicit argument (kept(name, fallback), same contract keptChecked already had), returning it ONLY pre-submit; 19 call sites across the batch-3/4 forms were migrated off ||, one of which (WeightForm.tsx) had silently made a falsy-but-valid default fall through — fixed by building the fallback argument with ??, not ||. PARTIAL because a ratchet BASELINE still admits the forms not yet converted.
rows.notes: React 19 resets an uncontrolled form once its action resolves, including when it returns an error, which wipes what the person typed. Batch 1 also found that keying a select off LIVE state remounts it on every pick, not only at the reset — the key must come from SOMETHING THAT CHANGES WHEN THE PICK DOES. kept() is the usual source (a value that round-trips through the action's FormData), but it is NOT the only sanctioned one: a value that is genuinely parent-owned and never submitted through the action at all — LegalMetadataFieldset's requirement-tier select, NoteForm's category select, FinalizeAdoptionForm's __appChoice/useFosterShortcut, and, since batch 4, 7 of PetForm's selects (sex, speciesGroup, speciesSubgroup, breed, trainingLevel, acquisitionMethod, microchipLocation) — keys off that PLAIN REACT STATE directly instead, with the SAME defaultValue+key shape, because kept() is simply not available to it (there is nothing for the action to echo back). The fence enforces the MECHANISM (a template-literal key that changes with the tracked value), not the SOURCE of that value. This notes field used to say 'the key must come from kept()' without qualification, which stopped being true the moment the first parent-owned-state select shipped and was never corrected here — it contradicted this row's own rule field, which already stated the exception correctly.

The defect it prevents has cost a gate twice: on 2026-08-30 two test:verified runs over ONE tree answered differently, with no worker crash and no broken file, because `const since = new Date()` in Node was compared against a column defaulted from Postgres's now() inside a Docker container whose clock had drifted. Two tests across three files, failing in OPPOSITE directions — one window too narrow to see its own row, two too wide and admitting the previous run's. THE RULE BANS THE SUBJECT, NOT A SPELLING, and the first draft got that wrong in a way worth recording: banning `new Date()` inside any comparison flags `gt(reminders.dueAt, new Date())` in pregnancy-flow.test.ts, which is CORRECT — dueAt carries no .defaultNow(), it is a future date the application computes, days away, where milliseconds of drift change nothing. A fence that reds a correct assertion teaches people to disable fences. So the column set is DERIVED from db/schema.ts at run time rather than hand-listed, and a new defaultNow() column is covered the day it is declared. Its own detector is exercised against a synthetic source rather than trusted, which is what caught two bugs in the detector on the first run: the fence was scanning itself and reporting its own fixtures, and the right-hand side pattern terminated on the paren inside `new Date()` so it could not match the single most common spelling of the defect. States its own limit: it cannot see a window built in a raw sql template.

Added 2026-09-11, long after the d7dbf25f7 snapshot, and the rule it guards was never written in prose so extraction had nothing to harvest: no citizen-facing file may name an Argentine state body in a way that implies it backs, operates or issues miMAR. It came out of a live finding — the landing hero carried 'República Argentina · Ministerio de Salud' above the H1, the footer repeated it over argentina.gob.ar/salud, and worst of all the phone credential printed 'República Argentina' in a slot whose style key is literally `footAuthority`, on the screen its own header calls 'the thing a funcionario is asked to accept as identification'. No convenio exists; the Mi Argentina one is still an unstarted prerequisite. It bans the SUBJECT rather than spellings — `Ministerio de <X>` matches a ministry nobody has typed yet — over 253 files, with two structural exemptions: a norm citation in the same sentence, and an explicit pending marker. Full https:// URLs are stripped before the name scan, so linking out to argentina.gob.ar stays legal; what is banned is a bare-text .gob.ar host or one carrying our own name. Floors at 180 files / 4 namings so a broken regex cannot go quietly green, and it was mutation-tested against the real tree, not a synthetic fixture.

Added 2026-09-18 with pilot item T1-P1 (PO decision D3): the pilot runs in the one environment that also holds the national demo seed, so no seed-tagged row may reach a govt or national reader of /gob. The rule lives in dim-interno:docs/handoff/rumbo-al-piloto.md, which the d7dbf25f7 snapshot does not harvest, so no row can cite a source for it without claiming a verifiedAt for a document the extraction never read. The exclusion itself lives inside the scope helpers (lib/metrics/scope.ts withoutSyntheticRows); what this fence holds is the bypass: every raw jurisdictionPairClause( call under lib/, src/ and app/ must apply the exclusion within 12 lines, carry a `synthetic: covered` tag naming a same-file function whose body is CHECKED to apply it, or a `synthetic: exempt` tag with a reason (tables with no seed marker). Floors at 30 call sites / 20 real applications and names the govt read paths it must see, so a sweep that stops matching cannot go quietly green; mutation-tested against the real tree. The behaviour is proven against the database in __tests__/gob-synthetic-exclusion.test.ts.

Added 2026-09-26 with the stage C review of the SDD change localidades-por-id. db:bootstrap pushes db/schema.ts before replaying db/migrations, so on a fresh database a migration's CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is skipped for every table schema.ts declares, and a CHECK written only in the migration never lands. The fence compares, for the authority-unit and place tables (0250, 0253/0254), every live CHECK name with the ones db/schema.ts declares, and pins place_repair_preimages (0251) as migration-only, so it cannot be moved into schema.ts without its CHECKs. Its canon row lands with the change's stage E, alongside the other localidades-por-id fences listed here.
